summary: SPAN destination oversubscription causing 54.94% loss at switch plus 2.12% drops at SIEM NIC - SIEM receives only ~45% of intended traffic, severely degrading detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: DIST-SW-02 SPAN destination Gi1/0/48 is oversubscribed: 2.22 Gbps mirrored from Gi1/0/1 forced into a 1 Gbps SPAN destination port. Switch egress buffers saturate at 100% load and tail-drop 13,060,680 packets (54.94% loss); bursts above 1 Gbps are lost first as SPAN has no burst buffering. The 10,714,260 packets that do egress still overrun the 1 Gbps SIEM eth1, which discards an additional 227,460 packets (2.12%) on capture.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM misses ~55% of flows/events before they reach detection - correlation, alerting and forensic coverage has major blind spots. Additional 2.12% NIC drops cause truncated flows and missed events even for traffic that survived SPAN, reducing SIEM efficacy despite its tolerant profile (needs_both_directions=false, needs_full_payload=false).

recommended_fix.why: TAP provides lossless, line-rate copy without SPAN copy-engine and destination-port oversubscription/burst drops. Place TAP at Gi1/0/1 into a packet broker with 10G ingress, then filter/aggregate to rate-shape to the 1G SIEM port to eliminate switch-level discards and reduce tool NIC overrun.
